cultural.vision_reason: The image shows a hand-woven strip-woven kente-style cloth in a blue-and-white checkerboard pattern with supplementary weft motifs, a classic Akan/Ashanti woven textile form consistent with the claimed ethnicity.

physical.title: cloth
physical.summary: Kente cloth, a rectangular man's garment, hand-woven in imported blue and white cotton, composed of 12 hand-woven narrow strips, hand-sewn together along the selvedges. The strips are designed and assembled alternately to form a chequerboard pattern; both ends have a variant design that serves as a border to the main field. Each narrow strip consists of a plain ground weave using white cotton in both warp and weft. A pattern is introduced in the weft by four pairs of uniform rectangular blocks in blue that frame varied geometrical patterns formed of discontinuous blue supplementary weft. The ends form a fringe.
